arabia.name: Arabia
arabia.one_liner: Open map where early aggression and map control decide the game.
notes: Wall early or expect constant Feudal pressure.
Forward golds and woodlines are common — scout them.
Camel and scout play are strong; archers can punish poor walls.

arena.name: Arena
arena.one_liner: Walled bases lead to booming, relic fights and Imperial Age swings.
notes: Fast Imperial or unique-unit push are common plans.
Control the relics in the center.
Monks, Onagers and trebs dominate the mid-to-late game.

black forest.name: Black Forest
black forest.one_liner: Dense forest corridors favor walling, booming and massive late-game armies.
notes: Wall the corridors and secure your side of the forest.
Expect post-Imperial treb and Onager wars.
Trade through a safe path is essential in team games.

nomad.name: Nomad
nomad.one_liner: No starting TC: race to build one, grab shore fish and secure resources.
notes: Villager scouting and early fights over TC spots are normal.
Fishing ships can give a huge early boost.
Protect your first Town Center at all costs.

migration.name: Migration
migration.one_liner: Teams start on separate islands; transports and naval timing unlock the mainland.
notes: Secure water before sending villagers across.
The mainland has the best gold and relics.
Fire Galleys and Demolition Ships can swing early water fights.

islands.name: Islands
islands.one_liner: Full water map: whoever controls the seas usually wins.
notes: Galley and Fire Galley rushes decide early control.
Protect fishing ships; raiding wins wars.
Late game revolves around Galleons, Cannon Galleons and island landings.

team islands.name: Team Islands
team islands.one_liner: Larger islands built for team games; dominate water then push together.
notes: Coordinate navy mass with your pocket.
Look for shallow crossings for early raids.
Trade cogs are safer than trade carts here.

coastal.name: Coastal
coastal.one_liner: Shallow shores allow fishing but the main fight is usually on land.
notes: Fish can give an eco edge but don't over-invest in docks.
Land rushes still work because the coast is shallow.
Scout for dock drops that threaten your shoreline.

continental.name: Continental
continental.one_liner: A large shared landmass with some water on the edges.
notes: Standard open-map openings apply.
Water is optional but can secure extra food.
Control the open center for relics and gold.

highland.name: Highland
highland.one_liner: Rivers and cliffs split the map; chokepoints matter.
notes: Control the shallows and bridges.
Walls on crossings stall aggression.
Relics often spawn in contested no-man's-land.

gold rush.name: Gold Rush
gold rush.one_liner: A huge central gold pile rewards whoever takes it first.
notes: Feudal military pressure on the center pays off.
Secure the gold with towers or a castle.
Don't let one player mine the whole pile uncontested.

baltic.name: Baltic
baltic.one_liner: A ring of water around a central land arena.
notes: Naval control raids shore economies.
The center is open and fights like Arabia.
Fire Galleys rule the early water.

mediterranean.name: Mediterranean
mediterranean.one_liner: A central sea divides teams; galleys control the tempo.
notes: Mass galleys early and deny enemy fishing.
Landings behind the navy are game-ending.
Late game favors Cannon Galleons if water is won.

archipelago.name: Archipelago
archipelago.one_liner: Many small islands; expand by sea and raid opponent islands.
notes: Secure nearby islands for resources.
Transports are vulnerable to navy; escort them.
Expect a long Imperial navy war.

scandinavia.name: Scandinavia
scandinavia.one_liner: Snowy coasts and dense forests favor mixed land and water play.
notes: Shore fish and deep-sea fish are both viable.
Forests make walling easy but also encourage early tower/ram.
Relic control on the mainland wins.

mongolia.name: Mongolia
mongolia.one_liner: Wide open steppe with scattered resources and lots of huntables.
notes: Cavalry and Cavalry Archers feel at home.
Hunt control can swing early eco.
Hard to wall; expect raids.

yucatan.name: Yucatan
yucatan.one_liner: Mesoamerican terrain with easy walls and central gold.
notes: Eagle warriors and archers are popular.
The jungle walls off easily.
Fight for the central gold and relics.

salt marsh.name: Salt Marsh
salt marsh.one_liner: Marshy wetlands with limited woodlines and shoreline fish.
notes: Wood is sparse; don't waste it.
Fish and shore fish extend your eco.
Expect mixed land-water fights.

oasis.name: Oasis
oasis.one_liner: A central lake surrounded by forests and resources.
notes: Woodlines ring the map; secure the outside.
The center is open for relics and raids.
Booming is common, but aggression punishes greed.

ghost lake.name: Ghost Lake
ghost lake.one_liner: A frozen central lake creates an open battlefield.
notes: The ice lake is a natural flanking route.
Herdables near the edges matter.
Standard open-map rules apply.

canals.name: Canals
canals.one_liner: Water canals cut through the land, creating natural chokepoints.
notes: Control the canals with towers and ships.
Land armies need to cross bridges.
Mixed land-water compositions shine.

crater lake.name: Crater Lake
crater lake.one_liner: Teams circle a central lake; control the rim and the fish.
notes: Water control raids all sides.
The rim is a natural defensive line.
Late game often becomes navy + treb.

fortress.name: Fortress
fortress.one_liner: Each player starts inside a fortified area with extra stone.
notes: Booming into Imperial is the default plan.
Siege and trebs break the walls.
Relic and gold control outside the bases decides the endgame.

rivers.name: Rivers
rivers.one_liner: Wide rivers with shallows split the map into zones.
notes: Control the shallows early.
Naval raids can hit exposed economies.
Expect defensive play until Imperial.

hideout.name: Hideout
hideout.one_liner: Players start behind partial palisade walls; early aggression still works.
notes: Walls are incomplete — exploit the gaps.
A quick tower or M@A can breach.
Booming is viable if you finish your walls.

hill fort.name: Hill Fort
hill fort.one_liner: Pre-built walls and towers make early rushes hard.
notes: Expect Fast Castle and boom strategies.
Siege is needed to break fortified positions.
Map control outside the walls wins.

steppe.name: Steppe
steppe.one_liner: Extra Town Centers in the middle spark a race to secure them.
notes: Send villagers to claim central TCs early.
Cavalry and scouts punish expanding villagers.
The player who holds the center snowballs.

african clearing.name: African Clearing
african clearing.one_liner: A wide savanna with herds and aggressive animal spawns.
notes: Control the herds and elephants for food.
Open terrain favors mobile armies.
Wall small sections, not the whole map.

amazon tunnel.name: Amazon Tunnel
amazon tunnel.one_liner: A narrow tunnel connects the two sides.
notes: Wall and hold the choke.
Boom behind the wall.
Siege and ranged units dominate the tunnel.

atacama.name: Atacama
atacama.one_liner: A dry open map with exposed gold piles.
notes: Gold is plentiful but exposed.
Cavalry and archers thrive.
Expect constant raiding.

bog islands.name: Bog Islands
bog islands.one_liner: Swampy islands with limited building room.
notes: Secure the nearest islands fast.
Wood is tight; plan docks carefully.
Navy decides who can expand.

cenotes.name: Cenotes
cenotes.one_liner: Open terrain dotted with water holes and shore fish.
notes: Shore fish help early eco.
The open land rewards aggression.
Dock drops are possible but risky.

city of lakes.name: City of Lakes
city of lakes.one_liner: Many small lakes create natural barriers and fish sources.
notes: Fish extend eco but require docks.
Lakes channel movement into chokepoints.
Mixed land-water play.

coastal forest.name: Coastal Forest
coastal forest.one_liner: Dense forests line the shore, blending land and water play.
notes: Forests make walling easy.
Fish give a small boost if contested.
Expect longer games than pure Arabia.

golden pit.name: Golden Pit
golden pit.one_liner: A deep central gold pit surrounded by open terrain.
notes: Fight for the pit from early Feudal.
Towers and castles on the rim control the gold.
Whoever mines the pit longest usually wins.

golden swamp.name: Golden Swamp
golden swamp.one_liner: Swampy ground with scattered gold and limited paths.
notes: Movement is restricted by shallow water.
Control the dry paths.
Booming is possible if you secure your side.

kilimanjaro.name: Kilimanjaro
kilimanjaro.one_liner: A large central mountain grants elevation advantages.
notes: Hold the high ground for range and attack bonuses.
The slopes create natural chokepoints.
Expect ranged and siege play.

mountain pass.name: Mountain Pass
mountain pass.one_liner: A single mountain pass links the two sides.
notes: Fortify the pass early.
Boom behind it.
Siege and ranged units decide the push.

nile delta.name: Nile Delta
nile delta.one_liner: A branching river delta with many small landings.
notes: Control the main water channels.
Transports can land almost anywhere.
Mix navy with mobile land units.

pacific islands.name: Pacific Islands
pacific islands.one_liner: Large ocean gaps between resource-rich islands.
notes: Secure your island, then contest neutral ones.
Naval superiority enables island hops.
Trade cogs are efficient if routes are safe.

sandbank.name: Sandbank
sandbank.one_liner: Shallow sandbanks connect islands for amphibious play.
notes: Demolition Ships punish clustered navies.
Villagers can walk across shallows.
Mixed navy and land aggression.

socotra.name: Socotra
socotra.one_liner: A very small island where players start dangerously close.
notes: Expect early aggression and villager fights.
There is nowhere to run.
Fast tower, archer or scout plays are common.

wolf hill.name: Wolf Hill
wolf hill.one_liner: Hilly terrain with aggressive wolves and scattered resources.
notes: Wolves can kill villagers early.
Hills give a permanent combat advantage.
Control the high-ground wood and gold.

acropolis.name: Acropolis
acropolis.one_liner: Teams start on plateaus separated by lower ground.
notes: High ground favors ranged units and siege.
The center holds relics and gold.
Drops off the plateau are risky but powerful.

rocky river.name: Rocky River
rocky river.one_liner: A rocky river with multiple crossings divides the map.
notes: Control the crossings.
The river slows but doesn't stop land armies.
Mixed aggression and defensive play.

sacred springs.name: Sacred Springs
sacred springs.one_liner: Scattered springs and relics encourage map control.
notes: Hold the central springs for water and relics.
Open enough for early pressure.
Good for booming with map control.

serengeti.name: Serengeti
serengeti.one_liner: Wide plains with large herds and few obstacles.
notes: Cavalry and Cavalry Archers dominate.
Herds provide fast food.
Hard to wall; expect raiding.
